claims.reason: Read as snoring together with breathing pauses, or snoring together with sleepiness, the title matches NICE 1.1.1: assess for OSAHS when 2 or more listed features (snoring, witnessed apnoeas, unexplained excessive sleepiness) are present. The patient-side step 'tell a doctor' is derived from that clinician-side recommendation; no snapshot addresses the public directly. The word 'Głośne' (loud) is not in the source but only narrows the title. If the title is instead read as 'loud snoring with pauses' OR 'sleepiness alone', the single-feature case is not backed (see W praktyce#1).

quotes.text: Take a sleep history and assess people for OSAHS if they have 2 or more of the following features:
witnessed apnoeas
unexplained excessive sleepiness, tiredness or fatigue

claims.reason: Backed: witnessed apnoeas, snoring and unexplained excessive sleepiness are all among the features for which NICE 1.1.1 says to take a sleep history and assess for OSAHS. Not backed: NICE sets the trigger at 2 or more of the listed features, while the sentence tells the reader to report each of the three on its own, including a single one; 'nasilone' (intensified) snoring is also not in the source, which lists plain 'snoring'. The NICE lines are addressed to clinicians, not to people reporting symptoms.

scope_gaps.note: NG202 is a UK (NHS) guideline for people over 16 and its recommendations are written for clinicians; the sentence names NG202 but not the population or country, which a reader might assume carries over to Poland.

Recommendation 1.6.1 pairs CPAP with lifestyle advice and says fixed-level CPAP; the cross-referenced TA139 line limits CPAP to adults with symptomatic moderate or severe OSAHS. The sentence says neither, but 1.6.1 itself states the recommendation without a symptom limit.
Source trigger is 2 or more listed features, assessed by a clinician; the sentence tells the reader to report any one of three, and says 'nasilone' chrapanie where the source says snoring.
Only 'do not drive when you feel sleepy' is in a source, and it sits in the NHS insomnia self-help list; stopping safely and using other transport are not in any snapshot.
No snapshot gives an instruction or reason against choosing a CPAP device or settings oneself; the sources only show a service-led care pathway.
Source stresses involvement of the person in decisions; the sentence names only the clinician as the one who chooses.
